sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Zelensky, evening address Sat Nov 7] The NABU/SAPO 'Operation Carthage' revelations are 'frankly shameful, absolutely unacceptable'. 'There have already been dismissals in the Security Service of Ukraine because of this, and there will be other personnel decisions.' He proposed legislation requiring ALL SBU employees to publicly declare their assets. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- NABU/SAPO] Senior SBU, National Police and Prosecutor General's Office officials allegedly shielded a criminal network running scam centres, drug trafficking, counterfeit currency and illegal cigarette production; the Khimprom cartel has expanded into Poland and is targeting Germany. [COUNTED] Two senior SBU officials already dismissed; a Ukrainian court on Friday ordered the arrest pending bail of a former SBU general in connection with the case.
sections.what_verified: 2 independent publisher families with declared tiers (Reuters T1, Ukrinform T2) plus the primary source itself (Zelensky's evening address). The News (no declared tier) reported with attribution but does not count toward corroboration.
sections.what_disputed: No convictions: the allegations are under investigation; the court action so far is arrest pending bail for one former SBU general. Domestic critics (Ukrainian-language social posts, high comment volume) argue the SBU answers directly to Zelensky himself, so a purge he orders is consolidation, not independent accountability. The probe is distinct from Operation Midas (Energoatom, see 1300-04) -- do not merge the two.
sections.why_matters: Wartime purge at the top of Kyiv's security state: the president calls his own service 'frankly shameful'. Pairs with the Midas conclusion (1300-04) as one anti-corruption wave -- but the two probes are different cases, keep them separate on screen.

totw_analysis: Our read: Wartime purge at the top of Kyiv's security state: the president calls his own service 'frankly shameful'. Pairs with the Midas conclusion (1300-04) as one anti-corruption wave -- but the two probes are different cases, keep them separate on screen. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Zelensky purging a rotten security service -- or tightening his grip on the one service that already answers to him?
